description: Malformed frames and the exact error each must produce. Every case here is a deterministic, byte-level input, so both implementations can be checked without a peer. A receiver that parses one of these successfully, or that reports a different code or severity, is non-conformant.

vectors.note: The first four bytes must be ASCII 'DLWP'. Nothing may be parsed before the magic is checked.
A version the receiver does not implement. The receiver must not attempt a best-effort parse (RFC-0001 section 10).
Version 1.0 defines no header extensions, so any header_length other than 24 is rejected. A receiver must not try to skip the extension bytes.
A zero header_length would make the header shorter than its own fixed prefix. Reject before reading the body.
A declared body larger than max_frame_bytes must be rejected by reading the header only, without allocating the declared size. 0xFFFFFFFF is the worst case an attacker can request.
The body begins with 0xFF, which is not a valid cbOR initial byte. A receiver must fail the frame rather than pass the bytes through to a per-message parser.
Indefinite-length encodings are forbidden so that a message has exactly one byte encoding (RFC-0001 section 3.2). 0xBF opens an indefinite map.
A value that fits one byte must be encoded in one byte. 0x18 0x05 encodes 5 in two bytes, which is non-canonical.
The protocol defines no floating-point fields, so every float encoding is rejected rather than coerced.
Tags are unused. 0xC2 opens tag 2, the positive bignum tag, which an attacker can use to smuggle a large integer past a naive length check.
0xFF is not a legal UTF-8 byte. A text key containing it must not be decoded with a replacement character.
HELLO must be the first frame of a session. A PING first is a protocol violation, not a warning.

RFC-0001 section 6.2 registers ERR_UNEXPECTED_MESSAGE as fatal, so the session ends. A peer that repeats AUTH has broken the state machine, and continuing would mean guessing which of the two proofs was authoritative.
An unregistered message type is answered with a recoverable error and the session survives, so that a newer peer cannot break an older one by sending a frame it has learned.
A registered message that the negotiated capability set does not include is refused, but the session continues.
An operation on a channel that was never opened is refused. Channel 0 is always open, so the frame must name a non-zero channel.
The agent advertises max_channels; opening one more must be refused without disturbing the existing channels.

A required key is absent, so the message cannot be executed. ERR_MALFORMED is fatal: the body failed validation and the peer cannot be trusted to resynchronise, so the connection closes rather than continuing in an undefined state.

A string where an integer is required is a schema violation, not a coercible input. ERR_MALFORMED is fatal for the same reason as the missing-key case: silent coercion of a coordinate is how a mis-tap bug is born, and continuing after a schema failure leaves both peers disagreeing about the request.
The forward-compatibility rule: an unknown key in a body must be ignored, not rejected. This is the one case where a 'malformed-looking' body is accepted.
Bits 4-7 of the flags byte are reserved. A receiver must ignore them rather than fail, so that the bits can be assigned later without a version bump.
A truncated frame is an I/O error, not a parse error: the receiver must wait for more bytes until the connection closes, then report ERR_IO.

sequence_vectors.note: The sequence number is session-global and must increase. A repeated value is treated as a replay attempt and is fatal, not recoverable.
A gap inside the 32-frame reordering window is legal on a lossy link and must not be reported as a replay.
A frame that falls outside the reordering window is rejected and terminates the session, because accepting it would let an attacker replay very old frames indefinitely.
